t: None of the funds made available in this Act may be used to amend the oath of allegiance required by section 337 of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1448).

fable.w: This is an appropriations rider that bars the use of funds to amend the oath of allegiance. The tempting reading is that an oath involves members of the public (naturalization applicants), but the section sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. It only restricts federal spending.
fable.s: None of the funds made available in this Act may be used to amend the oath of allegiance required by section 337 of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1448).

opus.w: This is a limit on how appropriated funds may be spent. It bars the use of funds to amend the oath of allegiance. It does not require or authorize consultation, comment, hearings, advisory bodies or lawsuits involving anyone outside the federal government. The mention of amending a legal requirement might suggest rulemaking, but the provision restricts action rather than granting regulatory authority.
opus.s: None of the funds made available in this Act may be used to amend the oath of allegiance required by section 337 of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1448).

qwen_chat.w: This section is a funding restriction that prohibits the use of appropriated funds for a specific legislative action (amending the oath of allegiance). It does not establish any process for consulting with, coordinating with, or receiving input from parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory committees, public hearings, comment periods, or consultation requirements mentioned.
qwen_chat.s: None of the funds made available in this Act may be used to amend the oath of allegiance required by section 337 of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1448).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section restricts how funds can be used, it implicitly involves a decision-making process that could include public input. However, the text itself contains no mechanism for consultation, comment, or coordination with any outside party. It is a simple prohibition on the use of funds for a specific purpose.
